title: I-10 is closed to bikes until Miller Rd in Buckeye
detail: ADOT bans bicycles on I-10 from Kolb Rd in Tucson (MP 270.6) to Miller Rd in Buckeye (MP 114.9), so Casa Grande to Phoenix is off limits. This line rides the Maricopa–Casa Grande Hwy to Maricopa, AZ 347 north (busy commuter traffic), Riggs Rd west through the Gila River Indian Community, then Laveen, Southern Ave and MC 85 (old US 80) into Buckeye. The shorter AZ 238 / Rainbow Valley line uses about 17 mi of desert track; skip it on a loaded bike.
source: ADOT Traffic Engineering Guidelines TGP 1030, Table 1030-A; azbikelaw.org; OSM surface tags

title: Maricopa → Laveen: about 25 mi of reservation roads
detail: Fill bottles in Maricopa (Walmart, QuikTrip). AZ 347 and Riggs Rd cross the Gila River Indian Community with few or no stores until Laveen and the West Valley suburbs, which have everything.

title: After rain, check washes and river crossings
detail: Desert roads here dip through washes, and the Hassayampa River crossing on Salome Hwy west of Buckeye floods. Never ride through moving water; check az511.gov. The I-10 shoulder (legal from Miller Rd west) bridges the Hassayampa if Salome Hwy is closed.

title: I-10 shoulder, Tonopah → Ehrenberg: legal, wide, full of tire wire
detail: Bikes are allowed on I-10 west of Miller Rd, and west of Brenda it is signed US Bicycle Route 90. The shoulder is wide but littered with steel belt wire from shredded truck tires: one rider had 10 punctures in a day (2024). Run sealant or tubeless, carry three or more tubes and patches. Stay on I-10 to exit 1 at Ehrenberg rather than the dirt Tom Wells Rd.

title: Tonopah → Quartzsite: water only at Burnt Well and Vicksburg Rd
detail: Tonopah exit 94 has a 24-h Pilot. Burnt Well rest area (8 mi west) has fountains and toilets. Exits 81, 69, 53 and 26 have nothing; Bouse Wash rest area is vending only. Exit 45 Vicksburg Rd has a 24-h Pilot and a Pride truck stop, the only food in 49 mi. Brenda's store is 1.5 mi up US 60 from exit 31.

title: Colorado River: bike bridge into California
detail: A separate bike and foot bridge on US Bicycle Route 90 crosses the river beside I-10 (gravel on the approaches); riders also report a bike lane on the I-10 bridge. Clocks go back an hour in California.

title: California I-10: bikes only from Mesa Dr (exit 232) to Dillon Rd (exit 146)
detail: I-10 through Blythe is closed to bikes: ride Hobsonway west and get on at Mesa Dr. Get off at Dillon Rd before Indio. The shoulder is about 10 ft, narrowing to 5 ft for about 2.5 mi west of Mesa Dr and 3 mi east of Chiriaco Summit. Caltrans is rebuilding I-10 from Wiley's Well to the Arizona line into winter 2026: expect lane shifts and closures.
source: Caltrans District 8 bike access map (2021) and existing-conditions data (2022)

title: Mesa Dr → Chiriaco Summit: 67 mi, no food, one water stop
detail: Last store: BB Travel Center/Chevron at exit 232 (24 h, 760-922-5109). Water only at Wiley's Well rest area (exit 222), then about 49 mi with none. Desert Center has nothing (the cafe closed in 2012); Lake Tamarisk Library, 1.8 mi north of exit 192, has a fountain Tue/Thu 10–6 and Sat 10–2. Carry 5+ liters from Blythe.
source: corridor services research 2026-11-01; Caltrans rest-area status

title: Chiriaco Summit → Dillon Rd: 26 mi, no water
detail: The Cactus City rest areas are closed for reconstruction until spring 2027. Next water: the Dillon Rd truck stops (Love's, TA) at exit 146.

title: San Gorgonio Pass: 2,300 ft up through the wind farms
detail: Palm Springs (about 450 ft) to Beaumont (about 2,600 ft) over 29 mi. The line follows CA 111, then the only legal piece of I-10 here (SR-62 junction to Haugen-Lehmann Way, exit 110), then Haugen-Lehmann Way into Cabazon. In a normal November the pass blows hard from the west about 3 days in 10; the forecast for Nov 5–8, 2026 is easterly, a tailwind. Whitewater rest area has water.
source: Caltrans District 8 bike map; NWS SGX forecast 2026-11-01; Whitewater RAWS climatology

title: Cabazon → Banning: the Morongo gap
detail: Johnson Lane (old US 60/70/99) ends in about 0.6 mi of dirt before Ramsey St. Morongo reservation roads may be gated (riders were turned away in 2024). OSM tags the I-10 shoulder from Malki Rd (exit 103) to Ramsey St (exit 102) as bike-OK, but Caltrans lists it closed: obey the signs at the on-ramp. On Ramsey St in Banning a cyclist was killed in March 2026; ride it in daylight.
source: OSM ways 925048796, 235324636; Caltrans D8; rider reports 2018–2024; bikinginla.com

title: Pacific Electric Trail: car-free but slow
detail: About 19 mi of concrete path from Rialto to Claremont. It crosses streets at push-button signals almost every block; Foothill Blvd (Route 66) runs parallel and is faster if you can take traffic.
